source_title: HawkEye 360 Successfully Launches Cluster 16 with Advanced Collection and Downlink Capabilities - PR Newswire
source_excerpt:
Dedicated satellite cluster introduces advanced antenna technology designed to support simultaneous RF collection and mission data downlink
HERNDON, Va. , Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- HawkEye 360, Inc. (NYSE: HAWK ), the global leader in signals intelligence data and analytics, today announced the successful launch of Cluster 16, a three-satellite cluster featuring advanced antenna technology designed to expand the flexibility and capacity of the Company's space-based RF collection architecture.
Cluster 16 launched aboard Rocket Lab's Electron rocket as part of the dedicated mission, "We're Not Hawking Around," from Rocket Lab Launch Complex 1 in New Zealand. Following deployment into an inclined orbit, HawkEye 360's space operations team successfully established communications with all three satellites and began the commissioning process.
The launches of Clusters 15 and 16, deployed just three days apart from launch sites on opposite sides of the world, demonstrate HawkEye 360's ability to manage a complex global launch cadence. With rideshare capacity increasingly constrained, the Company has secured launch opportunities through 2028 to maintain constellation continuity, preserve flexibility, and support evolving customer mission requirements.
Cluster 16 also includes advanced antenna capabilities supporting the simultaneous collection of multiple RF signal types and mission data downlink. Together, Clusters 15 and 16 are the first HawkEye 360 satellites designed with this capability, increasing collection opportunity while enabling faster delivery of mission data to customers.
Cluster 16 will provide dedicated capacity in support of a HawkEye 360 customer, demonstrating the Company's ability to configure and operate its space-based collection architecture around defined customer requirements and specific operational priorities.
"Cluster 16 advances both the capability and flexibility of our constellation," said John Serafini, Chief Executive Officer of HawkEye 360. "Simultaneous collection and downlink allow us to make better use of time on orbit, increasing our ability to collect signals while moving mission data to the ground more efficiently. Combined with dedicated capacity, this gives us another way to tailor our architecture around the operational needs of our customers."
The three satellites will operate in formation to detect, characterize and geolocate RF signals from space. Once commissioning is complete, Cluster 16 will expand HawkEye 360's capacity to support defense, intelligence and security missions with timely, shareable signals intelligence.
About HawkEye 360 HawkEye 360 is equipping defense, intelligence, and national security leaders with mission-critical signal intelligence to enable faster, better decision-making. By detecting, geolocating, and characterizing radio-frequency emissions worldwide, HawkEye 360 delivers trusted domain awareness and early-warning indicators to the U.S. Government and allied partners. Our space-based collection, proprietary signal processing, and AI-powered analytics transform knowledge of the RF spectrum into a strategic advantage. Proven by operational mission success, HawkEye 360 is redefining how signals intelligence strengthens national and global security.
